title: Judging Outputs - Correct, Incorrect, Unclear
summary: Students learn to give every AI output one of three verdicts - correct, incorrect or unclear - and to back each judgement with a reason they can check.
objectives: Identify, in a set of outputs, which are incorrect or unclear and say why.
Explain one signal that an output cannot be trusted as-is.
Recommend one action to take when an output is unclear.

sections.heading: Judging Outputs - Correct, Incorrect, Unclear
body: An answer can sound perfectly sure of itself and still be wrong. Today you become the judge who decides whether an output is correct, incorrect, or simply unclear - and you learn to back up every judgement with a reason.

sections.heading: I can…
items: I can sort outputs into correct, incorrect, and unclear.
I can give a reason for each judgement I make.
I can name one action to take when an output cannot be trusted.

terms.definition: The text or answer an AI tool produces after you give it a prompt.
The judgement you give an output: correct, incorrect, or unclear.
A trusted place, like a textbook or official website, you check an answer against.
When an AI tool states something made up as if it were a fact.
To check whether something is true using a reliable source.

sections.heading: Sounds right is not the same as is right
body: A language model writes by predicting which words usually come next. That makes its answers smooth and confident, but confidence is a writing style, not proof.
Your job is to separate 'sounds right' from 'is right' by checking the output against the task you set and a source you trust.

sections.heading: Three verdicts
body: **Correct** means the output matches the task and agrees with a trusted source.
**Incorrect** means it clashes with something you can check now - a fact, a number, or your instruction.
**Unclear** means it is vague, incomplete, or you cannot [[verify]] it yet, so it needs more checking before use.

sections.label: What to do with an output
sections.heading: Three verdicts, not two
sections.source: An output you have just read
sections.altText: One output leads to three possible verdicts: correct, incorrect, or unclear.

branches.label: Correct
branches.detail: You checked it against something else

branches.label: Incorrect
branches.detail: You found something that is wrong

branches.label: Unclear
branches.detail: You could not check it either way

sections.caption: **Unclear is a real verdict**, not a way of avoiding one. It records what you were unable to check, which is information the next person needs.

sections.label: Let's try it - hands-on
sections.heading: Let's try it - hands-on
body: You will triage three short outputs. For each, give a verdict and a six-word reason. Remember: a reason must point to a check, not a feeling.
items: Read the task the output was meant to answer.
Check it against the task and any source given.
Write your verdict: correct, incorrect, or unclear.
Add a short reason and, if needed, one action.

sections.heading: Think about it
items: Which signal most often warned you an output was not trustworthy?
When an output is unclear, is it safer to pause or to proceed?

sections.heading: My reflection
items: Write one thing you will now check before trusting an AI answer.
Describe a time a confident answer turned out to be wrong.

worksheet.title: Week 4 - Core - Worksheet | Judging Outputs - Correct, Incorrect, Unclear

questions.prompt: Triage three outputs. For each output, circle a verdict and write a checkable reason.
questions.stem:
This output is ... because when I checked it against ...
I cannot verify this because ...
questions.lookFor: Triages at least 2 of the 3 outputs correctly, and every verdict carries a reason tied to the task or to a source rather than to a feeling.

questions.prompt: Signal and action. Name one signal that an output cannot be trusted, and the action you would take.
questions.stem:
A warning signal is ...
My action would be ...
questions.lookFor: Any one checkable signal is acceptable - it contradicts the task, has no source, or contains a detail we cannot check - paired with a sensible action such as re-check, re-prompt, or ask a person.

questions.prompt: Output-triage record. Record your verdict, reason, and action for each output.
questions.lookFor: Each row pairs a verdict with a reason tied to task or source, and names a sensible action for any output judged unclear or incorrect.

questions.prompt: Exit ticket: flag these three outputs correct / incorrect / unclear and give a reason for each.
questions.lookFor: Correctly triages at least 2 of 3 outputs and gives a valid reason for each judgement. Push any 'it just feels wrong' towards a checkable reason.

questions.prompt: Challenge (stretch): find the single detail in a 'correct-looking' output that actually makes it incorrect, and explain how you spotted it.
questions.lookFor: Isolates the one subtle detail that flips the output from correct to incorrect, and explains the check that exposed it rather than describing a general impression.

formative.targets: Directly checks 'identifies when outputs are incorrect or unclear'
formative.check: Output-triage exit card: flag correct / incorrect / unclear with a reason each
formative.successCriteria: Correctly triages at least 2 of 3 outputs and gives a valid reason for each judgement.
